saints.name: St. Elizabeth Ann Seton
saints.title: Religious
saints.shortBlurb: A New York widow and convert who founded the Sisters of Charity and the first free Catholic school in the United States…
biography: Born in New York in 1774, the daughter of the physician Richard Bayley, Elizabeth was raised an Episcopalian and married the merchant William Magee Seton in 1794, bearing him five children. Ruined by bankruptcy, the couple sailed to Italy in 1803 for William's health, and he died of tuberculosis at Pisa, leaving her a widow at twenty-nine.

The kindness of the Filicchi family, Catholic merchants of Livorno, opened the Church to her, and on 14 March 1805 she made her profession of faith at Saint Peter's in New York, a step that cost her the regard of her Protestant relatives. In 1809 she settled at Emmitsburg, Maryland, and founded the Sisters of Charity of Saint Joseph, the first religious community of women founded in the United States.

From Emmitsburg her sisters ran an academy and a free school for poor girls, the seed of the American parochial-school system, whence her patronage of Catholic schools; her own early widowhood commends her to widows. She died of tuberculosis at Emmitsburg in 1821 and was canonized by Pope Paul VI on 14 September 1975, the first native-born citizen of the United States to be named a saint.
saints.knownFor: Founding American Catholic education and the Sisters of Charity.

sources.text: R. Seton (ed.), Memoir, Letters and Journal of Elizabeth Seton (1869; public domain)
